title: Animal fattening: introduction
competency: Explain animal fattening and the fattening systems in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: Feeding animals in one place for a set time to get the most high-quality meat.
A place where many cattle are fed concentrated feed.
A nutrient essential for growth; meat is a source.

en.text: Animal fattening is continuous feeding of animals in one place for a set time to get the most high-quality meat. Fattened bulls are not allowed to move far or work. Demand for meat is high and rising, so fattening is a profitable career. Ethiopia has three fattening systems: traditional, by-product-based and Hararghe.

screens.title: Brainstorming
screens.ask: What does animal fattening mean to you?
opts: Feeding animals well in one place so they gain weight for meat
screens.after: Fattening means keeping animals in one place and feeding them well to get more meat.

screens.title: 3.3.1 Introduction
paras: People need meat as a source of protein for growth.
High-quality meat comes from animal fattening.
Fattening is continuous feeding of animals in one place for a set time.
Fattening bulls do not move far or do farm work.

screens.title: A profitable career
paras: Fattened bulls give more and better meat.
Demand for meat is high and rising every year.
Producers cannot yet meet the demand.
So fattening brings profit in a short time.

screens.title: Fattening systems in Ethiopia
paras: Animals are home-grown or bought at local markets.
Breed, sex, maturity and age all matter.
table: Grass and some cereals; old oxen sold after ploughing
Maize, soy and other feeds; sometimes feedlots
Named in the book, not described

screens.text: Why are fattening bulls kept from moving far or working?
screens.why: Less movement and no work mean faster fattening.
screens.clue: Where does the energy from feed go?

screens.text: Demand for meat in Ethiopia is high and increasing.
screens.why: The book says producers cannot meet it.
These are the three systems in the book.

screens.text: Abebe has a strong market for meat and wants quick profit. What does the book suggest?
opts: Selling thin oxen right after ploughing
screens.why: Fattening gives more, better meat, and high demand makes it profitable in a short time.
screens.clue: Which business brings profit in a short time?

test.text: Fattening animals are kept in a specific place.
test.why: That is part of the definition.

test.text: How many fattening systems does the book name for Ethiopia?
By-product-fed cattle are mainly raised on grass only.
test.why: On maize, soy and other feeds.

test.text: In the traditional system, when do farmers sell oxen?

notes.text: The Hararghe fattening system is named but not described in the book.
"Too old to resist draught" probably means too old to continue ploughing work.
